triage.note: D1 (2026-08-23), promoting the S2 post-merge-gate debt row '`repo_hygiene` is listed and served as a filing fixture'. A fixture directory is one holding exactly one file, the filing; that rule lived only in app.py's request-time `_fixture_file`, while `/api/meta` listed every directory under evals/fixtures/ and `evals/oracle.iter_fixtures()` yielded the largest non-.md file of every directory. The check recomputes the single-file set INDEPENDENTLY of the predicate (`_single_file_dirs`, a plain walk) and requires that `list_fixtures()` (what /api/meta serves, hence the dropdown) and `iter_fixtures()` (what the bench times and `oracle.run_all` analyzes) both equal it, name for name and — for the oracle — file for file; and pins, as live text, that /api/meta actually serves `list_fixtures()`, that `_fixture_file` resolves through `fixture_file(d)`, and that app.py grows no second listing or predicate, because app.py imports fastapi and cannot be imported by the no-install CI jobs (ADR-003; same shape as `build_identity`'s `git_sha(ROOT)` pin). Two roots: the real tree, and the committed regression tree `evals/fixtures/repo_hygiene/fixture-discovery/`, whose `two-files/` (filing.htm + README.md) is the exact shape on which the three pre-D1 readers disagreed — /api/meta listed it, the oracle yielded its filing.htm, `POST /api/extract/fixture` 404'd it — and whose loose README beside the directories pins the is_dir filter. The suffix of the one file is deliberately not inspected: `_fixture_file` never did, and a lone non-filing file is refused by extract_items on content (measured: the regression tree's README.md -> `failed`/`normalization_collapse`, repo_hygiene's boilerplate-wire-values.html -> `unsupported`/`unsupported_form`) — a Debt row (Origin: D1) names the ceiling.
